assertions.quote: Your request cited PAY-88212, but the possible duplicate is PAY-88213, so the system returned a payment mismatch and no eligible refund amount.
assertions.reason: The reply correctly names the invoice (INV-2026-0142) and both settled payments, matching the observations (evidence 2 invoice amount 4900; evidence 3 shows PAY-88212 and PAY-88213 each 4900, both succeeded/settled; evidence 4 shows no refunds). However, it then treats the customer-cited locator PAY-88212 as a restriction, asserting an unsupported "payment mismatch" that yields "no eligible refund amount" and blocks refunding PAY-88213 — the very duplicate of that same invoice. The business rules make clear a payment reference is only a locator and binds a specific refund transaction only when the customer explicitly restricts it; the customer asked to refund the whole invoice's overcharge. Treating the cited receipt as a ban on refunding the other payment of the same invoice is exactly what this requirement forbids, so the identification is not consistent with the customer-authorized scope.
